summary: npm package ships iOS Mach-O implant kit behind an obfuscated fetch-and-eval JS loader
details: The package presents itself as a static-asset distribution helper but ships a heavily obfuscated JavaScript loader (a12i5u6l.js) that constructs module URLs from a runtime-configured base and passes fetched response text to new Function(body)() for in-process execution, and a second path that decodes two ~10KB embedded base64 blobs and injects them into the module cache via new Function(atob(blob)). The tarball also contains 19 arm64/arm64e iOS Mach-O binaries organized as agent_*, stager_*, and kbridge_* keyed to iOS versions 3.0-9.0, plus 04_c2/{new,old}/*.dylib files referencing 127.0.0.1 loopback C2 and the install name /usr/local/lib/SamplePayload.dylib. The Mach-O binaries link UIKit, Photos, Vision, CoreTelephony, CoreImage, and SystemConfiguration, and reference iOS private entitlements such as com.apple.private.security.storage.DiagnosticReports.read. Companion theme-new.min.js and theme-old.min.js (~230KB each) are opaque binary blobs rather than JavaScript. The iOS-native implant kit has no relationship to the advertised static-asset-distribution purpose, and the JS loader provides a generic remote-code-execution primitive against any consumer that imports it and supplies a base URL.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
